content.title: About
content.content: Biscuit cheese is a soft, creamy dairy product made from milk and cream, with added eggs and sugar, giving it a light, airy texture similar to a biscuit. It has a mild buttery flavor with a hint of sweetness and is commonly used in desserts and pastries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Biscuit cheese originated in Europe in the 19th century as a substitute for traditional curd in confectionery.
It is often used as a filling for rolls, cakes, and eclairs.
Unlike aged cheeses, biscuit cheese requires no maturation and is ready to eat immediately after production.
In some countries it is called “cheese biscuit” or “cream cheese” in a biscuit form.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Biscuit cheese provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Protein supports tissue repair and helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamins B2 and B12, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Compared with most hard cheeses, it contains less salt.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Contains lactose, so people with intolerance should limit consumption.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sugar is added for sweetness, making it unsuitable for low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to casein.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Biscuit cheese can be enjoyed on its own as a dessert, spread on bread, used as a filling for cakes, rolls, eclairs, and other pastries. It is also incorporated into creams and mousses to give a light, airy texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2 °C–6 °C in its original packaging. Once opened, it is best consumed within 7–10 days. Discard if it develops a sour smell or off‑color.
